Arbor_ImageSlider.description: Compare images, videos and audio of any size: flip through them with the slider, or wipe A against B. Videos and audio play in sync and keep their place when you switch, so an A/B comparison stays on the same moment.

images.name: images
images.tooltip: What to compare — images, videos or audio: a single value, a batch, a list or a tree. Every input grows a new slot; image batches give one slide per frame, audio batches one per clip (max 64 slides). Items of a named branch (a Load Folder folder, a storyboard scene) are labelled with its name.

labels.name: labels
labels.tooltip: Optional: a label for every item, matched branch by branch and item by item — one list serves every branch. It follows the branch name: Mei · Back, Kai · Close-up.

Arbor_ImageGrid.description: Lay images out as an XY comparison sheet: each branch is a row, each item a column.

images.name: images
images.tooltip: An image tree — or the plain images of a batch run, together with shape.

shape.name: shape
shape.tooltip: XY Lists' shape: pours plain images into rows × columns and labels them (rows by x, columns by y).

row_labels.name: row_labels
row_labels.tooltip: One label per row — a list, or a tree with one branch per row. Not needed when the tree or shape names its rows (XY Lists, Prompt Template, Cross Reference).

col_labels.name: col_labels
col_labels.tooltip: One label per column — overrides the labels taken from shape (which labels the columns when every row holds the same values, as in XY Lists).

captions.name: captions
captions.tooltip: One caption per cell — e.g. the prompts or seeds of a batch run: a tree shaped like the grid (item by item, branch by branch) or a flat list read cell by cell. Long captions wrap to three lines.

fit.name: fit
fit.tooltip: How pictures of different sizes fill a cell: fit (whole picture, bars around) · fill (covers the cell, edges cut) · original (no scaling) · stretch (fills the cell, distorted).

cell_size.name: cell_size
cell_size.tooltip: Longest side of a cell in pixels; 0 = the largest image's size.

gap.name: gap
gap.tooltip: Space between cells and around the sheet, in pixels.

font_size.name: font_size
font_size.tooltip: Label font size. Chinese labels render with a CJK font when one is installed.

path_labels.name: path_labels
path_labels.tooltip: Label rows with their branch path when there are no row labels or row names.

columns.name: columns
columns.tooltip: 0: one row per branch. N: every branch wraps after N cells — a flat list of 20 becomes 4 rows of 5; a branch's label spans all its rows. Column labels are left out when wrapping.

label_direction.name: label_direction
label_direction.tooltip: Row labels: auto (horizontal while they fit in two lines, otherwise standing up) · horizontal · vertical. Standing up, Chinese stacks upright; other text reads bottom to top.

caption_style.name: caption_style
caption_style.tooltip: below: under each cell (the sheet grows to fit) · overlay: on a dark bar across the bottom of the picture.

0.name: image
0.tooltip: The comparison sheet as one image.

Arbor_VideoGrid.description: Image Grid for video: each branch is a row, each clip a column, all playing in sync in one labelled video.

videos.name: videos
videos.tooltip: A video tree — or the plain videos of a batch run, together with shape. An image batch counts as one clip (its frames played at the grid's frame rate).

shape.name: shape
shape.tooltip: XY Lists' shape: pours plain videos into rows × columns and labels them (rows by x, columns by y).

row_labels.name: row_labels
row_labels.tooltip: One label per row — a list, or a tree with one branch per row. Not needed when the tree or shape names its rows.

col_labels.name: col_labels
col_labels.tooltip: One label per column — overrides the labels taken from shape.

captions.name: captions
captions.tooltip: One caption per cell — e.g. the prompts or seeds of a batch run: a tree shaped like the grid (item by item, branch by branch) or a flat list read cell by cell. Long captions wrap to three lines.

fit.name: fit
fit.tooltip: How clips of different sizes fill a cell: fit (whole clip, bars around) · fill (covers the cell, edges cut) · original (no scaling) · stretch (fills the cell, distorted).

cell_size.name: cell_size
cell_size.tooltip: Longest side of a cell in pixels; 0 = the largest clip's size. Keep it modest — the grid video is width × height of all cells.

gap.name: gap
gap.tooltip: Space between cells and around the grid, in pixels.

font_size.name: font_size
font_size.tooltip: Label font size. Chinese labels render with a CJK font when one is installed.

path_labels.name: path_labels
path_labels.tooltip: Label rows with their branch path when there are no row labels or row names.

fps.name: fps
fps.tooltip: Frame rate of the grid video; 0 = the highest frame rate among the clips. Every clip keeps its own speed.

audio.name: audio
audio.tooltip: none: a silent grid · mix: every clip's sound mixed together (loudness kept below clipping).

columns.name: columns
columns.tooltip: 0: one row per branch. N: every branch wraps after N cells — a flat list of 20 becomes 4 rows of 5; a branch's label spans all its rows. Column labels are left out when wrapping.

label_direction.name: label_direction
label_direction.tooltip: Row labels: auto (horizontal while they fit in two lines, otherwise standing up) · horizontal · vertical. Standing up, Chinese stacks upright; other text reads bottom to top.

caption_style.name: caption_style
caption_style.tooltip: below: under each cell (the sheet grows to fit) · overlay: on a dark bar across the bottom of the picture.

0.name: video
0.tooltip: The grid as one VIDEO (H.264 MP4 in the temp folder) — save it with Save by Path or Save Video, or compare it in the Compare Viewer.

Arbor_SmartResize.description: Resize by longest / shortest side, megapixels, a box or a scale factor, snapping both sides to a multiple (8 / 16 / 64 for latent-friendly sizes).

mode.name: mode
mode.tooltip: How the target size is chosen. Only the fields for the chosen mode are shown.

mode_size.name: size
mode_size.tooltip: Target length of the longest / shortest side, in pixels.

mode_megapixels.name: megapixels
mode_megapixels.tooltip: Target area in megapixels (1.0 ≈ 1024 × 1024); aspect ratio is kept.

multiple_of.name: multiple_of
multiple_of.tooltip: Round both sides to a multiple of this — use 8 / 16 / 64 for diffusion models.

method.name: method
method.tooltip: Resampling filter. lanczos is sharpest; area is best for strong downscaling.

allow_upscale.name: allow_upscale
allow_upscale.tooltip: Off: never make the image larger than it is.

mask.name: mask
mask.tooltip: Optional mask, resized (and cropped) exactly like the image.

0.name: image
0.tooltip: Resized image.

1.name: mask
1.tooltip: Resized mask (all ones when no mask was given).

Arbor_BatchPick.description: Pick frames from an image batch or a video by index, inclusive range or slice. Order and repeats are kept.

images.name: images
images.tooltip: Image batch — or a video, whose frames are picked from.

indices.name: indices
indices.tooltip: Comma / space separated: 0, 2, -1 (from the end), 3-5 (inclusive range), 1:8:2 or ::2 (Python slices).

0.name: images
0.tooltip: The picked frames, as one batch.

Arbor_SplitGrid.description: Cut a grid picture — a storyboard sheet, a contact sheet, a sprite sheet — into its panels, row by row. Gutters and margins are found and left out; without them the picture is cut evenly.

image.name: image
image.tooltip: One sheet, or a batch / list of sheets — each sheet becomes one branch.

rows.name: rows
rows.tooltip: How many rows of panels the sheet has.

find_gutters.name: find_gutters
find_gutters.tooltip: Look for gutters and margins — lines of one flat colour — near every cut and leave them out, so panels that are not quite even still come out clean. Off: cut into even parts.

inset.name: inset
inset.tooltip: Pixels shaved off every panel edge, to drop the soft edge of a gutter.

0.name: data
0.tooltip: Every panel as plain data, in reading order (left to right, top to bottom) — panels may differ by a few pixels in size.

1.name: tree
1.tooltip: One branch per sheet, its panels in reading order.

Arbor_LoadMedia.description: Pick pictures, videos and audio from anywhere on disk and group them into named branches — several Load Image nodes in one, using the system's own file dialog, with thumbnails. Files are used where they are; nothing is copied.

files.name: files
files.tooltip: The list (kept as text): '# name' starts a named group, an empty line a new group, every other line is a file — an absolute path, output/… (ComfyUI's output folder), arbor:… (Arbor's sample media) or relative to the input folder. Edit it in the node's Text view, or fill it with Add….

0.name: files
0.tooltip: Everything, one branch per group, named after it — the data tree: Cross Reference, Tree Branch, the Compare Viewer, Save by Path, a Panel.

1.name: names
1.tooltip: File names without extension, like files — handy as captions or for Save by Path.

2.name: images
2.tooltip: Every picture (IMAGE) as plain data, in list order — connect straight to image nodes, which run once per picture.

4.name: audio
4.tooltip: Every audio clip (AUDIO) as plain data.

Arbor_LoadFolder.description: Load every picture, video or audio file in a folder; with subfolders on, each folder becomes a branch, named after it — the folder structure turns straight into a data tree.

folder.name: folder
folder.tooltip: An absolute path; output/… for ComfyUI's output folder; arbor:… for Arbor's sample media; any other relative path is inside the input folder. The folder icon at the end of the box picks it with the system's folder dialog.

kind.name: kind
kind.tooltip: What to load: images (IMAGE) · videos (VIDEO — read lazily, nothing is decoded until a node needs the frames) · audio (AUDIO). Each kind has its own file pattern.

kind_pattern.name: pattern
kind_pattern.tooltip: File name patterns separated by spaces, e.g. *.png *.jpg or *.mp4 *.mov or *.wav *.flac.

subfolders.name: subfolders
subfolders.tooltip: On: each subfolder (and the folder itself, if it has matching files) becomes a branch. Off: only this folder.

sort.name: sort
sort.tooltip: name = natural order (img2 before img10); modified = oldest first.

limit.name: limit
limit.tooltip: Maximum number of files in total; 0 = all. Pictures and audio are held in memory, so limit large folders.

0.name: files
0.tooltip: The pictures / videos / audio as a tree, one branch per folder, named after it — Image Grid labels its rows with the names, the Panel and Compare Viewer show them.

1.name: names
1.tooltip: File names without extension, same layout — handy as labels or for Save by Path.

2.name: folders
2.tooltip: Folder names as plain data, one per branch.

Arbor_SaveByPath.description: Save a tree keeping its structure — pictures as PNG, videos as MP4, audio as FLAC, text as TXT: one subfolder (or filename part) per branch, named after the branch when it has a name, with optional names per file.

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: What to save — a tree, a list or a single value. Picture batches are saved frame by frame, audio batches clip by clip; other values are skipped.

filename_prefix.name: filename_prefix
filename_prefix.tooltip: Where to save: a folder / prefix inside ComfyUI's output folder (arbor/run), output/…, or an absolute path such as D:/renders/run — the folder icon at the end of the box picks the folder. Outside the output folder only while ComfyUI listens on this computer alone. Supports %date%-style variables.

layout.name: layout
layout.tooltip: subfolders: prefix/0-1/000.png (a named branch: prefix/0-1 · name/000.png) · flat: prefix_0-1_000.png. A plain list (one unnamed branch {0}) goes straight under the prefix: prefix/000.png · prefix_000.png

names.name: names
names.tooltip: Optional file names, matched to the files item by item (e.g. Load Folder's names or a Prompt Template).

0.name: paths
0.tooltip: Saved file paths, in the same tree layout (and with the same names).

Arbor_Panel.description: Inspect anything, or type data in. Connected: shows the input and passes it through. Unconnected: each line you type is an item, an empty line starts a new branch and a `# title` line names it.

data.name: data
data.tooltip: Anything — a data tree, a native list, an image, a number… Leave it unconnected to type data instead.

text.name: text
text.tooltip: The typed data (used when nothing is connected). Edited in the panel itself.

parse_numbers.name: parse_numbers
parse_numbers.tooltip: Typed values: lines like 7 / 3.5 / true become INT / FLOAT / BOOLEAN. The 123 / abc button in the panel.

multiline.name: multiline
multiline.tooltip: Text mode: the whole text is one item. The Lines / Text switch in the panel.

0.name: data
0.tooltip: The data as a native list: downstream nodes run once per item (a single item runs once).

1.name: tree
1.tooltip: The data as a tree — for Arbor nodes, keeps the branches.

Arbor_NumberSlider.description: Grasshopper-style number slider: drag the bar to set a value between min and max, click it to type. A step of 1 gives whole numbers.

value.name: value
value.tooltip: Current value — set it on the bar.

min.name: min
min.tooltip: Lower end of the range (click the left number under the bar).

max.name: max
max.tooltip: Upper end of the range (click the right number under the bar).

step.name: step
step.tooltip: Values snap to min + k × step: 1 = whole numbers, 0.05 = steps of 0.05, 0 = continuous. Also sets how many decimals are shown.

0.name: data
0.tooltip: One output for every number input: connects to INT inputs (steps, seed) and FLOAT inputs (cfg, denoise) alike. Whole numbers come out as INT, others as FLOAT.

Arbor_NumberSequence.description: A list of numbers, defined by a step (series) or by both ends (range).

mode.name: mode
mode.tooltip: series: start, start + step, … · range: start → end split evenly. Only that mode's fields are shown.

mode_step.name: step
mode_step.tooltip: series: difference between neighbours (negative counts down).

mode_steps.name: steps
mode_steps.tooltip: range: number of equal parts — you get steps + 1 numbers.

as_int.name: as_int
as_int.tooltip: Round to whole numbers — for seeds, steps, sizes.

0.name: data
0.tooltip: The numbers as plain data — connect straight to cfg, steps, seed… (the node runs once per number) or to any Arbor input.

Arbor_SplitText.description: Split text into items — one per line or separator; an empty line starts a new branch. table reads a pasted spreadsheet: one branch per column.

text.name: text
text.tooltip: The text. Can be typed or connected from any STRING output.

separator.name: separator
separator.tooltip: What separates items inside a paragraph: newline, comma, semicolon or |. table: rows copied from a spreadsheet or a CSV — cells split by tabs (or commas when there are none, quotes allowed), the first row names the columns, every column becomes a branch.

blank_line_branches.name: blank_line_branches
blank_line_branches.tooltip: Paragraphs separated by an empty line become branches {0}, {1}, …

0.name: data
0.tooltip: Every item as plain text data (paragraphs one after another).

1.name: tree
1.tooltip: The items as a tree: one branch per paragraph.

Arbor_PromptTemplate.description: Fill {a} {b} … in a template from trees. Cross builds every combination as a grid-ready tree; zip pairs them branch by branch and item by item, like Grasshopper.

template.name: template
template.tooltip: Text with placeholders {a} … {f} (and, in zip mode, {name} — the branch's name). Placeholders without a connected value stay as they are. Several lines are fine.

mode.name: mode
mode.tooltip: cross: every combination — rows = {a}, columns = the last variable used. zip: branches paired in order, items one by one (longest list), the tree keeps its branches and names.

vars.name: vars
vars.tooltip: Values for {a}, {b}, … — a tree, a list or a single value. Each connection adds the next letter.

vars_a.name: a
vars_a.tooltip: Values for {a}, {b}, … — a tree, a list or a single value. Each connection adds the next letter.

vars_b.name: b
vars_b.tooltip: Values for {a}, {b}, … — a tree, a list or a single value. Each connection adds the next letter.

vars_c.name: c
vars_c.tooltip: Values for {a}, {b}, … — a tree, a list or a single value. Each connection adds the next letter.

vars_d.name: d
vars_d.tooltip: Values for {a}, {b}, … — a tree, a list or a single value. Each connection adds the next letter.

vars_e.name: e
vars_e.tooltip: Values for {a}, {b}, … — a tree, a list or a single value. Each connection adds the next letter.

vars_f.name: f
vars_f.tooltip: Values for {a}, {b}, … — a tree, a list or a single value. Each connection adds the next letter.

0.name: data
0.tooltip: Every filled prompt as plain data — connect straight to a text encoder (it runs once per prompt).

1.name: tree
1.tooltip: The prompts as a tree (cross: one branch per combination of the outer variables — ready for Image Grid).

Arbor_Expression.description: Evaluate a formula for every item, like Grasshopper's Expression: x and y are matched branch by branch in order and item by item (longest list).

expression.name: expression
expression.tooltip: Python-style formula, e.g. x * 2 + 1, x > 3, upper(x), x if i % 2 else -x.

x.name: x
x.tooltip: First value — a tree, a list or a single value. Leave both empty for a single constant result.

y.name: y
y.tooltip: Optional second value, matched to x branch by branch in order and item by item; whichever is shorter repeats its last branch / item.

0.name: data
0.tooltip: Every result as plain data.

1.name: tree
1.tooltip: Results as a tree, with the paths of the input whose paths are longest (x on a tie). Comparisons give booleans — ready for Dispatch.

Arbor_Random.description: Seeded shuffle, or pick a number of items (with or without repeats). Same seed, same result.

tree.name: data
tree.tooltip: Items to shuffle or pick from — plain data or a tree (handled branch by branch).

mode.name: mode
mode.tooltip: shuffle: reorder everything · pick: choose count different items · pick (repeats): choose count items, repeats allowed.

count.name: count
count.tooltip: Items to pick per branch (ignored by shuffle).

seed.name: seed
seed.tooltip: Random seed — the same seed always gives the same result.

per_branch.name: per_branch
per_branch.tooltip: On: every branch separately. Off: all items as one list.

0.name: data
0.tooltip: The shuffled / picked items as plain data.

1.name: tree
1.tooltip: The shuffled / picked items, branch by branch.

Arbor_Collect.description: Gather any values — pictures, masks, latents, audio, video, text — into data: one branch per input, named, or all in one list.

inputs.name: inputs
inputs.tooltip: Anything. Every connection adds a slot. A list fills its branch with all its items; a tree keeps its own branches under {i;…}.

inputs_input0.tooltip: Anything. Every connection adds a slot. A list fills its branch with all its items; a tree keeps its own branches under {i;…}.

Arbor_XYLists.description: From values to a batch run: every combination of x, y (and z) as aligned plain data — wire them into ordinary nodes and they run once per combination — plus the shape of the runs. With only x connected it flattens any tree into plain data.

x.name: x
x.tooltip: Values for the rows — or any tree to flatten into plain data.

z.name: z
z.tooltip: Optional third parameter: becomes the columns, rows become x × y.

mode.name: mode
mode.tooltip: cross: every combination · zip: item by item (longest list, the last item repeats); the shape keeps the branches of the longest input (x, then y, then z) — one row when that is a plain list.

0.name: x
0.tooltip: x of every run — connect to any widget input (cfg, steps, seed…). The node it feeds runs once per combination.

2.name: z
2.tooltip: z of every run (empty values when z is not connected).

3.name: shape
3.tooltip: Layout of the runs: connect to Image Grid (rows × columns) or Construct Tree (back into a tree). Each row is named after its x value and its items are the column values, so Image Grid labels itself. With only x, it is x's own tree.

Arbor_TreeToData.description: Every item of a tree as plain data, so ordinary nodes run once per item — plus its shape, to put the results back.

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: The tree to run over — every item becomes one run of the nodes it feeds.

0.name: data
0.tooltip: Every item as plain data, in branch order: connect to any ordinary node (a text encoder, a sampler input…) and it runs once per item.

1.name: shape
1.tooltip: The tree itself: connect to Construct Tree or Image Grid to put the results back into the same branches, with their names.

Arbor_ConstructTree.description: Build a tree from plain data: put every item on one path, or — with shape connected — pour the items back into another tree's branches.

data.name: data
data.tooltip: Any value or plain data (a native list), e.g. the results of a batch run.

path.name: path
path.tooltip: Branch path for the items when no shape is connected, e.g. {0} or {0;2}.

shape.name: shape
shape.tooltip: A tree whose branch layout to copy — XY Lists' shape, or the tree you flattened. The item counts must match.

split_batch.name: split_batch
split_batch.tooltip: Split IMAGE / MASK / LATENT batches into one item per frame first.

0.name: tree
0.tooltip: The tree.

Arbor_ReshapeTree.description: Change how items are grouped into branches — Grasshopper's Graft, Flatten, Simplify, Flip Matrix, Shift Paths and Renumber in one node.

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: A data tree, or any value / list (becomes branch {0}).

mode.name: mode
mode.tooltip: graft: every item its own branch · flatten: everything in one branch · simplify: drop path indices all branches share · flip matrix: swap rows and columns · shift paths: drop path indices, joining branches that meet · renumber: {0}, {1}, {2}, … in order.

mode_path.name: path
mode_path.tooltip: flatten: path of the single output branch, e.g. {0}.

mode_offset.name: offset
mode_offset.tooltip: shift paths: −1 drops the last index (undoes graft), +1 the first.

0.name: tree
0.tooltip: The resulting tree.

Arbor_TreeBranch.description: Pick branches by path (e.g. {0;1}) or by name — several separated by commas — or, when path is empty, one by index (Grasshopper's Tree Branch).

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: A data tree, or any value / list (becomes branch {0}).

path.name: path
path.tooltip: Paths such as {0;1} or branch names such as Mei, separated by commas (Mei, Kai); leave empty to pick by index.

index.name: index
index.tooltip: Branch index when path is empty; wraps around, −1 = last branch.

0.name: tree
0.tooltip: A tree with only those branches, paths and names kept.

1.name: data
1.tooltip: Their items as plain data, branch after branch — straight into a node that runs once per item.

Arbor_TreeStatistics.description: Branch count, item count, depth and the list of paths.

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: A data tree, or any value / list (becomes branch {0}).

0.name: branches
0.tooltip: Number of branches.

3.name: paths
3.tooltip: One line per branch: path and item count.

Arbor_ListItem.description: Pick items from every branch by index, list, range or slice — Grasshopper's List Item and Sub List in one node.

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: A data tree, or any value / list (becomes branch {0}).

index.name: index
index.tooltip: Which items: `0` · `-1` (last) · `0, 2` · `1:4` (slice, end excluded) · `2-5` (range, end included) · `::2` (every other). A connected number works too, or a tree of indices: its branches pair with the list's in order, so every branch picks its own items.

wrap.name: wrap
wrap.tooltip: Out-of-range indices wrap around the branch length. Off: they give an empty value, so branches stay aligned.

0.name: tree
0.tooltip: The picked items, branch by branch.

1.name: data
1.tooltip: The picked items as plain data, branch after branch: index k on a tree of sheets gives frame k of every sheet as one list — straight into a node that runs once per item.

Arbor_Dispatch.description: Split items by a true / false pattern: A keeps the true ones, B the false ones — use A alone to cull a list (Grasshopper's Dispatch and Cull Pattern).

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: A data tree, or any value / list (becomes branch {0}).

pattern.name: pattern
pattern.tooltip: Typed repeating pattern ('T F', 'true,false', '1 0 1', 'TFT'), or connect BOOLEAN values / a boolean tree (e.g. Expression 'x > 2'), whose branches pair with the list's in order, like Grasshopper.

0.name: A
0.tooltip: Items where the pattern is true — the kept items when culling.

1.name: B
1.tooltip: Items where the pattern is false.

Arbor_Partition.description: Chop every branch into chunks of size items: {p} → {p;k} (Grasshopper's Partition).

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: A data tree, or any value / list (becomes branch {0}).

size.name: size
size.tooltip: Items per chunk; the last chunk may be shorter.

0.name: tree
0.tooltip: The resulting tree.

Arbor_Repeat.description: Repeat items: each gives aabbcc, whole gives abcabc. With a shape connected, every branch is stretched to the item count of its matching branch instead — Grasshopper's Longest List.

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: A data tree, or any value / list (becomes branch {0}).

count.name: count
count.tooltip: How many times (ignored while a shape is connected).

mode.name: mode
mode.tooltip: each: repeat every item in place · whole: repeat the whole list. With a shape: each spreads the items evenly (a a b b), whole cycles them (a b a b).

shape.name: shape
shape.tooltip: Optional tree to match. Branches pair in order (the last one repeats); each branch gets as many items as its partner and takes its path, so the result lines up with the shape item by item.

0.name: tree
0.tooltip: The resulting tree.

Arbor_SortList.description: Sort every branch — numbers first (by value), then text (alphabetically) — or reverse it.

tree.name: tree
tree.tooltip: A data tree, or any value / list (becomes branch {0}).

order.name: order
order.tooltip: ascending · descending · reverse (keep the items, flip their order).

0.name: tree
0.tooltip: The resulting tree.

Arbor_CrossReference.description: Every combination of A × B, branch by branch, like Grasshopper's Cross Reference: branches pair in order (the shorter tree repeats its last branch) and the result takes the paths of the input with the longest paths. With group on: rows = A, columns = B.

group.name: group
group.tooltip: Off (default): Grasshopper's Cross Reference — all combinations stay in the branch. On: one sub-branch per A item, the same as grafting A first — grid-ready (rows = A, columns = B).

0.name: A
0.tooltip: A repeated for every B.
